questions.text: How long have you been experiencing night sweats, and how severe are they — do they drench your clothes or bedding?
questions.purpose: Characterise duration and severity; drenching night sweats are a clinically significant constitutional B-symptom

questions.text: Have you also had unexplained weight loss or persistent fever alongside the night sweats?
questions.purpose: The triad of fever, night sweats, and weight loss (B-symptoms) is a red flag for lymphoma or haematological malignancy

questions.text: Could this be related to menopause — are you female and aged 40 or above, or perimenopausal?
questions.purpose: Menopausal hot flushes/night sweats are the most common benign cause in women in the appropriate age group

questions.text: Do you have symptoms suggesting tuberculosis — persistent cough, haemoptysis, or known TB contact?
questions.purpose: TB is a major infectious cause of night sweats requiring specific investigation

questions.text: Do you have HIV, are on HIV treatment, or have you had any recent high-risk exposures?
questions.purpose: HIV and HIV-associated infections (MAC, CMV, opportunistic infections) cause night sweats

questions.text: Do you have any enlargement of lymph nodes, spleen, or liver?
questions.purpose: Lymphadenopathy or organomegaly with night sweats points to haematological or infective aetiology

questions.text: Are you taking any medications such as antidepressants, tamoxifen, or other drugs that commonly cause sweating?
questions.purpose: Many medications cause night sweats as a side effect and are reversible causes
